claims.text: NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 is a predominantly single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy in its baseline state.
Increasing Ta content to an optimal level and annealing at 600–900 °C will nucleate fine hcp precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The proposed treatment will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale hcp precipitates in an originally single-phase BCC matrix.
The resulting BCC matrix will be ductile and metastable.
Nanoscale hcp precipitates impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation strengthening.
The ductile BCC matrix preserves plasticity in the precipitate-containing alloy.
Heterogeneous BCC–hcp interfaces deflect and blunt cracks.
Crack deflection and blunting at BCC–hcp interfaces improve fracture resistance.
Microstructural refinement helps produce a more favorable Young’s modulus.
The treated dual-phase alloy will have greater yield strength than the single-phase BCC baseline.
The treated alloy can achieve a yield strength above 800 MPa.
The treated alloy will maintain or improve ductility relative to the single-phase BCC baseline.
The treated alloy can achieve plastic strain above 15%.
The treated alloy will have a Young’s modulus better aligned with structural requirements.
The treated alloy will have greater fracture resistance than the single-phase BCC baseline.
Improved fracture resistance will be manifested by increased energy absorption and crack deflection during in situ fracture testing.
Precipitate coarsening or heterogeneous phase distributions, including brittle intermetallic formation, can compromise ductility and fracture resistance.
In situ high-resolution TEM monitoring during annealing can prevent precipitate coarsening.
